questions.qtext:
Consider a relation R(A, B, C, D, E) with the following set of FD’s.
F = {A → BC, AB → D, B → E, AC → D, C → B, D → E, A → C}
Which of the following are correct canonical covers (minimal FD’s) of the given set of functional dependencies?

options.text: {B → E, AC → D, D → E, C → B, A → C}
{A → D, C → B, A → C, B → E, D → E}
{B → E, AB → D, D → E, C → B, A → C}
{A → D, B → E, D → C, C → B, A → C}

questions.solution:
(b)
To check which options are valid canonical covers,
• The closure of each option is equal to the closure of original FD’s.
• There are no extraneous attributes.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
Consider a relation R(A, B, C, D, E, F) with the following functional dependencies.
{AB → C, C → D, AF → B, B → E}
Which of the following is/are true?

options.text: Relation is in 2NF, but not in 3NF.
{B → E} is a partial dependency, so relation violates 2NF.
The FD : {C → D} violates BCNF, as C is not a super key.
Replacing {C → D} with {AB → D} and keeping all other FD’s, make the relation BCNF complaint.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
AF is the only candidate key.
• No partial dependency exist, so relation is in 2NF.
• There exist transitive dependency from AF → B → E hence relation is not in 3NF.
• Replacing FD : {C → D} with {AB → D} do not make relation in BCNF.

questions.qtext: In a relation R(A1, A2, ..... An). The set of attributes Σ ⊆ R{A1, A2, ..... An} is called a superkey if :

options.text: Σ+ = R{A2, A3, ..... An} and Σ may not minimal.
Σ+ = R{A1, A2, ..... An – 1} and Σ is minimal.
Σ+ = R{A1, A2, ..... An} and Σ may not minimal.
Σ+ = R{A1, A3, ..... An} and Σ is minimal.

questions.solution:
(c)
[Superkey = Candidate key + Optional attributes]
A candidate key is always a super key but a super key may not be a minimal candidate key (it may have extra attributes).

questions.qtext:
In the context of index file structures used in database, consider the following three alternatives for storing data entries in an index.
A1 : Each data entry with key k is an actual data record with search key k.
A2 : Each data entry is a pair (k, rid), where rid is the record id of data record with search key k.
A3 : Each data entry is a pair (k, rid-list), where rid-list is the list of all record id’s with search key k.
Which of the following statements are correct?

options.text: A1 act as a specialized fill organization that can substitute a sorted or unsorted file.
Both A2 and A3 decouple the index structure from the underlying file organization used for storing data records.
A3 improves space utilization compared to A2, but requires entities to be of fixed length.
A3 while saving space, reduce redundancy but introduce variable length data entries.

questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
(a) If the index directly stores full data record (A1) there’s number need to go elsewhere for the actual data, so it behave like a file itself, not pointer based index.
(b) A2 and A3 have entries point to record. So it does not matter how or where the actual record one stored.
(c) A3 size depends on rid-list size, depends on how many records share the same key.
(d) Instead of repeating (k, rid) for every record (A2) A3 groups all rid together saving space.

Consider the attribute set in R(A, B, C, D, E, G) and the FD set:
{AB → C, AC → B, AD → E, B → D, BC → A, E → G}
Consider the following decomposition of R.
D1 : R1(AB), R2(BC), R3(ABDE), R4(EG)
D2 : R1(ABC), R2(ACDE), R3(ADG)
Which of the following is true?

options.text: D1 , D2 are lossless and not dependency preserving.
D1 is lossy, D2 is lossless and D2 is not dependency preserving but D1 is.
D2 is lossy, D1 is lossless and D1 is not dependency preserving but D2 is.
D2 is lossless, D1 is lossy and D1, D2 are not dependency preserving.

questions.solution:

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements regarding database normalization:
S1 : Every decomposition which satisfies 3NF is always lossless and dependency preserving.
S2 : Every decomposition which satisfies 2NF removes partial dependency but transitive dependency may still exist.
S3 : Every decomposition which satisfies BCNF is always lossless, but may/may not functional dependency preserving.
S4 : ∃ Relation whose decomposition is in BCNF, lossless and dependency preserving.
Number of incorrect statements is/are ________.

NAT
questions.solution:
2
• Every relation possible to decompose 3NF, LLJ and DP.
• NPA transitively determine by SK : (not allowed in 3NF).
• Every relation possible to decompose into BCNF with LLJ.
• Not every relation possible to decompose into BCNF with LLJ and DP.
